pr.title: Name an older daemon from `trip screen`, and say how to switch back after a mismatched upgrade
pr.head: 2d2bbd3f3b7d8f27d1d602359dc23330db3ccc5b

summary: trip runs a long-lived daemon that holds every terminal session, and the trip command is a client that sends it one request per invocation. Because trip upgrade never restarts the daemon, a newer client often talks to an older daemon. When that daemon cannot decode a request, it closes the connection without replying. The previous pull request, #31, taught the client to turn that close into one line naming the older daemon and saying when it moves to the new version.
This pull request follows up two suggestions from that review:

1. trip screen now reports an older daemon. It used to treat a close before any reply as success, so against an older daemon it printed nothing and exited 0. A current daemon always replies to a screen request before it closes, so a close before the first reply is now an error, and the older-daemon line explains it. trip log keeps the old behavior, because a current daemon also closes without replying when a log has no events.
  2. A mismatched upgrade says how to switch back. When trip upgrade installs a build that reports a version other than the release tag's, the installer has already made that build current. The error now says so and, when the installer kept a previous link, gives the ln -sfn command that points current back at it.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Older daemon: a running daemon whose version, recorded in ~/.trip/daemon.json, is lower than the client's.
  • current and previous: symlinks in ~/.local/share/trip. current names the installed version, and ~/.local/bin/trip runs through it. previous names the version current named before the installer last switched it to a different version.
  • Mismatch: the release tag says one version and the build it installs reports another.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open P2 finding: when the mismatched build reports the version that was already running, the installer leaves previous on an older version, and the suggested command would downgrade.
  • Two suggestions: explain an empty trip log against an older daemon on stderr, and test trip screen --watch of a session that ends.

groups.title: trip screen and an older daemon
groups.kicker: A close before the first reply is now an error for trip screen, but not for trip log.
intro: get_screen reads replies from the daemon until the connection closes. In watch mode it prints each new screen, so a close after a reply means the session ended and is a normal exit. A close before any reply only happens when the daemon refused the request, so that case now fails with unexpected frame. main.rs already passes every request's error through explain_daemon_failure, which turns unexpected frame into the older-daemon line when the daemon is older.
get_log cannot make the same change. The daemon's GetLog handler writes nothing when there are no events to show and then closes, so an empty log and a refusal look identical to the client.

files.note: Adds the close-before-first-reply branch to get_screen, and rewrites the comment on explain_daemon_failure to name trip log as the exception.

checks.text: Read the daemon's GetScreen handler: in both modes it writes ScreenData or Error before it closes, and in watch mode it writes the first screen before it subscribes, so first is false by the time a session ends.
trip shutdown also treats a close as success, printing daemon stopped, but Shutdown is a unit variant every daemon decodes, so the comment's claim holds for requests an older daemon can refuse.

groups.title: Switching back after a mismatched upgrade
groups.kicker: The mismatch error says the build is current and gives the way back.
intro: trip upgrade runs the release's own install.sh and then checks what ~/.local/bin/trip --version reports. By the time that check fails, the installer has already switched current to the new build. The new previous_version reads the installer's previous link, and the error appends run ln -sfn <previous> ~/.local/share/trip/current to switch back when that link names a different version from the one installed.

files.note: Builds the switch-back clause from previous_version() and adds it to the mismatch error.

checks.text: When the mismatched build reports the version already running, the installer reinstalls over that version and leaves previous on the version before it. The message then says to "switch back" to that older version, which is a downgrade. Offering the command only when previous names VERSION would fix it.
Compared with link_version in install.sh: both reduce an absolute target to its last path component, and the installer keeps the directory previous names, so the suggested target exists.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: End-to-end checks for both messages, and the README's Upgrading section.
intro: tests/upgrade_e2e.py runs the release binary in a temporary HOME. It now checks that trip screen against its fake older daemon prints the older-daemon line, and that a real current daemon still answers trip screen and returns an empty trip log with exit 0. It also pins the exact mismatch message with and without a previous link.

checks.text: Ran python3 tests/upgrade_e2e.py on the head: it ends with all upgrade checks passed.
The fixture points previous at 0.0.9, a version the client never ran. A real installer would point it at the version the upgrade switched away from.

files.note: Describes the switch-back command and names trip log as the request that cannot report an older daemon.
